article.title: US moves to restrict China's remote access to advanced SI chips
paras: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Mandarin article.

The U.S. Commerce Department announced new restrictions Monday on remote access to advanced super intelligence (commonly referred to as artificial intelligence), chips and servers, technology. The new restrictions are meant mainly to stop Chinese companies that are getting around U.S. limits on chip sales by using or renting computer time in other countries.
The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) issued an interim final rule developed at the direction of the Treasury Department and the National Security Council.

Under the new rule, U.S. chip suppliers will need government permission before selling advanced chips to data centers that let Chinese companies rent or use large amounts of that computing power. The limit is roughly equal to the power of about 330 of Nvidia’s more advanced chips.
It also requires licenses for chip exports to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil, which Commerce says pose a higher risk that chips will be diverted.

The rule requires data centers, overseas chip manufacturers and chip exporters to conduct enhanced due diligence on customers, including determining whether they are directly or indirectly owned or controlled by Chinese state-owned enterprises or entities in Macau.
In addition to China, the restrictions cover Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Russia.

The Commerce Department said the rule is intended to bring safeguards governing remote access to advanced computing capabilities into closer alignment with existing controls on the physical shipment of sensitive American technology.

The department said the United States remains the global leader in advanced computing and super intelligence technology and is committed to promoting the legitimate commercial use of American technology worldwide. But it warned that rapid advances in cloud computing and super intelligence infrastructure have made it increasingly possible to access advanced U.S. computing capabilities remotely, including through data centers in countries not subject to U.S. export restrictions.

China's Foreign Ministry criticized the new restrictions, accusing Washington of interfering in China's trade and technology cooperation with other countries. Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said Tuesday that the United States was "overstretching the concept of national security."
He added that the measures violated understandings reached between the two countries, warning that "China will take necessary measures to firmly safeguard its legitimate rights and interests."
Chairman of the House Select Committee on China and Republican Representative John Moolenaar of Michigan, welcomed the announcement of restrictive measures by the U.S. government.
In a statement Monday, Moolenaar said the rule “sends a message to the CCP that America is serious about closing dangerous export control loopholes China has been exploiting for years.”

Moolenaar called the measure an important step toward preventing sensitive chips from falling into the wrong hands, strengthening U.S. national security laws and protecting America's leadership in the race for super intelligence.

In January, the House passed the Remote Access Security Act, which seeks to restrict foreign adversaries, including the Chinese Communist Party, from obtaining access to U.S. technology through cloud computing services.

Rush Doshi, who served as director for China affairs on the National Security Council during the Biden administration, said in a post on X that the Trump administration's new remote-access rule was driven by the controversy surrounding Jensen Huang. The former Nvidia CEO resigned last week after admitting to an extramarital affair with a businesswoman who U.S. authorities believe was recruited by Chinese intelligence, according to The New York Times. China rejects the report.
The announcement also comes amid differences within the Trump administration over how to approach Megaspeed.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC last week that the Treasury, State and War departments, along with the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative, had favored placing Singapore-based Megaspeed on the Commerce Department's Entity List for months.

The list identifies foreign individuals and entities considered to pose risks to U.S. national security or foreign policy interests. U.S. companies generally need a license to export certain items to listed entities, with the licensing policy varying by entity and product.
Bessent said the Commerce Department controlled the decision, adding that it was up to the department to explain its internal process.

President Donald Trump told reporters Monday that there were "two different views" on how to approach the issue. He described one as favoring a friendlier approach and the other as being willing to risk a confrontation. Trump said both positions were acceptable and that he understood both sides.

Trump departed Monday for the Philippines to attend a special U.S.-ASEAN summit in Manila. He is also scheduled to travel to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' informal meeting and hold talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday.
zh: 美國採取行動，限制中國對先進半導體晶片的遠端存取
編者註：本文翻譯自美國之音（VOA）的原文（中文）。
美國商務部週一宣布，針對遠端存取先進超級智慧（通常稱為人工智慧）、晶片及伺服器等技術實施新的限制措施。這些新限制主要旨在阻止中國企業利用或租用其他國家的電腦運算時間，藉此規避美國對晶片銷售的限制。
工業與安全局（BIS）發布了一項臨時最終規則，該規則是根據財政部及國家安全委員會的指示制定的。
根據新規定，美國晶片供應商在向允許中國企業租用或使用大量運算能力的資料中心銷售先進晶片前，必須取得政府許可。此限制大致相當於約 330 顆 Nvidia 較先進晶片的運算能力。
此外，該規定還要求對出口至新加坡、馬來西亞、印尼、泰國及巴西的晶片申請許可證，美國商務部表示，這些國家存在較高風險，可能導致晶片被轉用。
該規定要求資料中心、海外晶片製造商及晶片出口商對客戶進行加強盡職調查，包括查明客戶是否直接或間接由中國國有企業或澳門實體擁有或控制。
除了中國之外，這些限制措施還涵蓋古巴、伊朗、北韓和俄羅斯。
美國商務部表示，這項規定旨在使規範遠端存取先進運算能力的保障措施，與現行針對美國敏感技術實體運輸的管制措施更加一致。
該部門表示，美國在先進運算與超級智慧技術領域仍居全球領先地位，並致力於在全球範圍內推動美國技術的合法商業應用。 但該部門警告，雲端運算與超級智慧基礎設施的快速發展，使得遠端存取美國先進運算能力變得日益容易，包括透過不受美國出口限制的國家所設的資料中心。
中國外交部批評了這些新限制措施，指責華府干涉中國與其他國家的貿易及科技合作。外交部發言人郭家坤週二表示，美國正在「過度擴張國家安全概念」。
他補充說，這些措施違反了兩國達成的共識，並警告稱：「中國將採取必要措施，堅決維護自身的合法權益。」
眾議院中國問題特別委員會主席、密西根州共和黨眾議員約翰·穆勒納爾，對美國政府宣布實施限制性措施一事表示歡迎。
穆勒納爾週一在一份聲明中表示，這項規定「向中共傳達了一個訊息：美國正認真致力於堵住中國多年來一直利用的危險出口管制漏洞。」
穆勒納爾稱，這項措施是防止敏感晶片落入不法之徒手中、強化美國國家安全法律，以及維護美國在超級智慧競賽中領導地位的重要一步。
今年一月，眾議院通過了《遠端存取安全法案》，該法案旨在限制包括中國共產黨在內的外国敵對勢力，透過雲端運算服務取得美國技術。
曾於拜登政府時期擔任國家安全委員會中國事務主任的拉什·多希（Rush Doshi），在 X 平台上發文表示，川普政府頒布的新遠端存取規定，是受黃仁勳（Jensen Huang）所引發的爭議所驅動。 據《紐約時報》報導，這位前英偉達執行長上週承認與一名女商人有婚外情，而美國當局認為該名女商人係受中國情報機構招募，他隨後辭職。中國方面否認了這項報導。
這項聲明發布之際，川普政府內部對於如何處理梅加斯皮德一事也存在分歧。
財政部長史考特·貝森特上週向CNBC表示，財政部、國務院和戰爭部，以及美國貿易代表辦公室，數月來一直主張將總部位於新加坡的Megaspeed列入商務部的「實體清單」。
該清單列出了被認為對美國國家安全或外交政策利益構成風險的外國個人及實體。美國企業向清單所列實體出口特定物品時，通常需要取得許可證，而許可證政策會因實體及產品的不同而有所差異。
貝森特表示，這項決定由商務部掌控，並補充說，該部門應負責說明其內部程序。
總統唐納德·川普週一告訴記者，對於如何處理此問題，存在「兩種不同的觀點」。他將其中一種描述為傾向採取更友善的態度，另一種則願意冒著對峙的風險。川普表示，這兩種立場都可以接受，而且他理解雙方立場。
川普週一啟程前往菲律賓，將在馬尼拉出席一場美越東盟特別峰會。他還預計將前往中國深圳，參加亞太經濟合作組織（APEC）領導人非正式會議，並於週四與中國國家主席習近平舉行會談。
